comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The cookie-consent bar on sportsdle.com ("We value your privacy", Accept All / Reject All / Cookie Settings) is an inline-styled fixed bottom overlay that survived the full AdGuard baseline, so a domain-scoped hiding rule was added for it and verified in the proxy experiment (banner gone, page intact). The rule goes to AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt at the end of the "Cookies - Specific basic" region, before line 17005. ## Rule `sportsdle.com##div[style*="position: fixed"][style*="z-index: 9999"]` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, which the AdGuard filter policy assigns to the AdGuard Cookie Notices (Annoyances) filter; the policy's Cookie Notices section states hiding or blocking the corresponding script is usually sufficient. No run-instruction rule closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion, and not a scam/phishing page. The fix is a domain-scoped element-hiding rule; no gate, scroll lock or consent-dependent feature was observed on the page. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! SECTION: Cookies - Specific basic`, before [line 17005](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a341349a321a1c55a33686836cf2e9963859bedd/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L17005). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45727360816 Automated analysis against filters at `a341349`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

Reproduced:⁠ with filtering, player.antyradio.pl keeps its #⁠player, podcast column and "POSŁUCHAJ RÓWNIEŻ" sections stuck on "Trwa ładowanie ..." spinners; unfiltered, the page shows the Agora/OneTrust consent dialog and, once accepted, loads that content with a pre-roll ad. Since the ad-block detector script never appears in the captured requests (antiAdblockDetected=false, no wall in the DOM) and the level OneTrust allowlist rule did not restore the consent dialog, this needs a maintainer rather than a new rule from this run.

## Still visible after the rule

- #⁠player / main radio player at top — The main player area is a large black panel containing only a small centered loading spinner; no player controls, track info or playable audio UI appear.
- Podcast column left of the Kanały muzyczne grid — The left podcast column remains blank with a loading spinner; no podcast cards or links are rendered.
- POSŁUCHAJ RÓWNIEŻ section — Below the 'POSŁUCHAJ RÓWNIEŻ' heading the section is a large blank area with a centered loading spinner; the station list/content is absent.
- POSŁUCHAJ RÓWNIEŻ stations section, between the section heading and the footer — The stations section is an empty reserved loading area with a centered animated spinner placeholder and no station tiles or playable station content. This repeats the reporter-defined endless loading / withheld-content symptom in the 'POSŁUCHAJ RÓWNIEŻ' section.
- Top #⁠player panel, full-width black area directly under the main navigation — Centered loading spinner in a large otherwise empty player area; no track metadata, player controls, or audio content appears, matching the reporter-described endless 'Trwa ładowanie ...' player state.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Anti-adblock walls:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The issue is filed as an 'Anti Adblock Script' report, and the captured requests for player.antyradio.pl show no detector script (experiments report antiAdblockDetected=false; no wall, popup or ad-block message exists in the DOM), so no anti-adblock rule may be written by this run. Run instruction:⁠ "A notice that the ad blocker breaks the site's consent banner is a cookie-consent problem, not an anti-adblock wall" - what the page shows is a consent/ad-gated player that never leaves its loading placeholder, not a wall, so the resolution touches the shared consent/ad framework and is a maintainer decision. Run instruction:⁠ "Do not block a shared video-player or ad-framework SDK ... that collateral risk is human-review territory" - the gate on this page is driven by the site's ad module on gfx-player.radiozet.pl (Yieldbird/GPT) plus the OneTrust consent SDK, both shared by the whole Eurozet player family.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"89da144076ee421ced5d3a39c0271a4421e1cbad2c6bf811ea2fe1a092fae503"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — thegirlinspired.com replaces its article with a Raptive ad-block-recovery wall ("An ad blocker is preventing this page from loading", help address thegirlinspired@⁠error-report.com); the page's inline Raptive scripts set __adblocker then load https:⁠//html-load.com/bundle.js, whose decoded strings point at error-report.com. The CLI baseline never shows the wall because it redirects ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js to a no-op ($redirect is unsupported in the reporter's Safari-based AdGuard Mini), so the rule could not be verified — apply_rule phase A was refused with HTTP 403. Candidate for review:⁠ extend the existing ||html-load.com^ family in BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt with ||html-load.com^$script,domain=thegirlinspired.com; alternatively add the domain to the Raptive scriptlet group on lines 106-107 of that file.

## Candidate for review

`||html-load.com^$script,domain=thegirlinspired.com`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not judge the candidate:⁠ phase A navigation failed twice with 'Phase A navigation failed (http_blocked):⁠ main document returned HTTP 403', and the host instructed to finish analysis-only. Beyond that refusal, the reported wall is product-specific:⁠ the CLI baseline applies ||ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js$xmlhttprequest,redirect=noopjs, so the page's __adblocker cookie is never set and the html-load.com bundle is never requested in either phase; full-page vision over the loaded baseline page returned reporterSymptomPresence 'absent' (instanceCount 0). $redirect is not supported by SafariConverterLib, the execution model of the reporter's AdGuard Mini for Mac, which is why the wall appears for them but not in this environment.

## Missing information

- Safari "Script/scriptlet rules" limitation section not served by lookup_rule_guidance: The linked AdGuard filter-syntax document lists a heading "#⁠#⁠#⁠#⁠ Script/scriptlet rules" under "#⁠#⁠#⁠#⁠ SafariConverterLib {#⁠safari-converter-lib}", but three lookup_rule_guidance calls (topics compatibility and scriptlet, queries naming Safari/SafariConverterLib/scriptlets) never returned that section — they returned the basic-rules and HTML-filtering limitation sections instead. For this report the answer matters:⁠ the reporter uses AdGuard Mini for Mac (Safari content blocker, where the doc states $redirect is NOT supported), and I need to know whether scriptlet (#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet) rules run in that product before choosing between the existing Raptive scriptlet group (BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt lines 106-107) and a plain network rule as the fix.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45732310103

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"edf1ad5dd48adafbeb23752492672a98881655770ac5083887a1e9bc7b309244"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On kofunkan.pref.kumamoto.jp the Social Media filter hides the AddToAny share buttons and leaves the pale-gray "この記事をシェアする" band as an empty leftover strip. The repository already has a shared 88-domain `.c-share` rule in SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt (line 11782), and adding this domain fixes the leftover in the browser experiment, but the bound vision review refused to confirm it, so the rule goes to a maintainer for review.

## Candidate for review

`kofunkan.pref.kumamoto.jp##.c-share`

SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule returned environmentExperiment=inconclusive with no failedCandidateChecks, but the bound vision review rejected the candidate as symptom 'not_resolved' with ad layout residue present. That rejection is contradicted by the experiment's own structure facts (`.c-share` visible 48px in phase B, hidden 0px in phase C, document height 3537→3489) and by independent reads of the same phase-C artifacts, which show no 'この記事をシェアする' text and identify the remaining pale band as the site's own 前の記事へ/次の記事へ navigation row. domChecks measured the leftover space as the transparent wrapper's 30px/20px padding with nothing painting a background. The rule appears to fix the reported leftover share strip but could not be confirmed by the bound visual review.

## Still visible after the rule

- 記事本文の展示写真の下、前の記事へ／次の記事へナビゲーションの上 — 展示写真の直後から前後記事ナビの間に、共有ラベルや共有ボタンが見当たらない淡いグレーの空帯が残っている。候補後も共有ウィジェットの内容は表示されず、空白のみが残っている。
- Full-width pale-gray band directly below the mascot photo and above the 前の記事へ / 次の記事へ navigation — The reserved social-share band is present but appears empty; no social-share buttons or usable share controls are visible in it.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45737622040

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — higo-canvas.com article pages carry an AddToAny social share bar (div.c-share, label 「この記事をシェアする」) that the reporter annotated and filed as a Social Widget; the same `.c-share` selector is already hidden by the shared 88-domain rule at SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt:⁠11782, so the fix is to add higo-canvas.com to that rule (higo-canvas.com first in the domain list). The candidate `higo-canvas.com##.c-share` verified in the before/after experiment:⁠ widget hidden, page integrity intact, no leftover residue. ## Rule `higo-canvas.com##.c-share` ## Policy rationale The repository's policy closes paywall reports and hands anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script to a maintainer; neither applies here — the target is an AddToAny social share widget, which the AdGuard Social filter exists to block. The policy excludes widgets that are part of the site's functionality or content (comments, embedded posts, polls, login widgets) and links to the site's social pages; a 「この記事をシェアする」 share bar is none of these and the same `.c-share` widget is already filtered on 88 other domains. No self-promotion, paywall, or anti-adblock rule of the run instruction blocks this fix, so rule generation is allowed. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/951ebfa7d4cbb4c44a7349ad3bfeb50e600a398e/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 11782](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/951ebfa7d4cbb4c44a7349ad3bfeb50e600a398e/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L11782). ## Screenshots

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The Yahoo!フリマ topics article still showed its social share widget — the "この記事をシェアする" block above the article navigation and the share icon row in the header — because the Social filter only hides the individual Facebook/X/LINE share links, leaving the wrapper and label behind; the new rule paypayfleamarket.yahoo.co.jp#⁠#⁠.SocialButton in SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt hides the whole widget and was verified in the browser experiment (symptom resolved, page intact, no residue). ## Rule `paypayfleamarket.yahoo.co.jp##.SocialButton` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy only closes paywalls and hands anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script to a maintainer; a social share widget is neither, so rule generation is allowed. The target is a social widget in the site's own served HTML and the fix is a cosmetic rule for the Social filter, which the repository keeps in SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4118494c794f59175814ed53f1ddf43a3960b9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 10723](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4118494c794f59175814ed53f1ddf43a3960b9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L10723). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On sanyu.co.jp the "この記事をシェアする" share strip stays visible as an empty labeled bar because the Social Media filter already hides its Facebook/Twitter/LINE buttons. Extending the existing shared rule `…##.c-share` in SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt (line 11782) with sanyu.co.jp hides the whole strip, and the validated experiment confirmed the symptom is gone with page integrity intact. ## Rule `sanyu.co.jp##.c-share` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's close/hand-off rules cover paywalls, anti-adblock walls (no detector request was captured here) and self-promotion; none applies:⁠ the captured requests are social-plugin loaders, and the target is a social share widget. The element falls under the AdGuard Social Media filter's stated purpose (blocking third-party social share buttons/widgets on third-party sites). AdGuard filter policy's social-media limitations (comments, embedded posts, polls, social login, links to the site's own social pages) do not apply — this is a plain share strip. Maintainer rule on shared rules:⁠ extend the existing shared rule instead of writing a new one; the .c-share rule is a class-name shared rule, not a group kept for one project. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4c39d682c0e34dbac56cc09181180ca6a4b43f24/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 11782](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4c39d682c0e34dbac56cc09181180ca6a4b43f24/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L11782). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45737309102 Automated analysis against filters at `4c39d68`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.fit.ac.jp the AdGuard Social filter's generic rules hide the LINE/X/Facebook share links but leave the "この記事をシェアする" block as an empty gap, exactly the area the reporter circled; the candidate fit.ac.jp#⁠#⁠.c-research-sns hides that leftover container and was verified to clear the empty gap with page integrity intact. ## Rule `fit.ac.jp##.c-research-sns` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy closes paywalls and anti-adblock reports without a captured detector script; this report is neither — the page loads fully and no wall, gate or consent message is involved. The filter policy for social media filters states that third-party Like/Share widgets are blocked by the Social filter, which the generic rules in AdGuard Social filter already do here; hiding the empty container that blocking leaves behind is in scope for the Social filter. The advertiser-facing policy clauses (self-promotion, paywalls, anti-adblock) do not apply, so the report is open to rule generation. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4c39d682c0e34dbac56cc09181180ca6a4b43f24/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 14141](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/4c39d682c0e34dbac56cc09181180ca6a4b43f24/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L14141). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45737419494 Automated analysis against filters at `4c39d68`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — retroexplore.com shows a first-party orestbida-style consent bar (div#⁠cc-main ⁠> .cm-wrapper .cm--bar.cm--bottom, "Cookie Consent" with Manage preferences / Reject all / Accept all) plus its dimming overlay; no CMP host is in the network log, so hiding is the fix. Validate `retroexplore.com###cc-main` passed (symptom resolved, page integrity intact), and since `###cc-main` already exists as a 195-domain shared rule, the maintainer should add `retroexplore.com` to that rule's domain list at AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 156 (comment `! ###cc-main`). ## Rule `retroexplore.com###cc-main` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice (label T:⁠ Annoyance, reporter filter 'AdGuard Cookie Notices'); the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter policy states it blocks cookie notices and that 'in most cases, simply hiding or blocking the corresponding scripts is sufficient'. No repository policy rule closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, and not self-promotion. The fix extends an existing shared rule for the same selector instead of adding a site-specific duplicate, matching the maintainer rule on shared rules. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/8a66d317dfb7e390957d3b85702ded8a9f5b7996/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 156](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/8a66d317dfb7e390957d3b85702ded8a9f5b7996/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L156). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report claims jcrew.com becomes slow and unresponsive with AdGuard, but both reporter screenshots show identical intact pages and, under the filtered baseline, the homepage loaded completely (58 headings, 97/97 images, no hidden or empty element, no ad slots) with only tracker/RUM/ad-tag requests blocked. No filter-attributed breakage reproduced and no unfiltered session exists here for a timing comparison, so no rule is proposed and the report needs a maintainer decision.

## Missing information

- No unfiltered control session is obtainable in the adguard_cli environment, so an "AdGuard on vs off" performance claim cannot be compared: The reporter's complaint is purely a performance claim ("When Adguard is enabled, the page becomes very slow and unresponsive"), with no visible defect in either of the two screenshots. In the locked adguard_cli environment, launch_browser with extension:⁠"none" rejects a settings object and, when launched without settings, still returns a session whose get_applied_rules lists the same 11 filtering rules acting on https:⁠//www⁠.jcrew.com/ (the CLI proxy filters every session), so no genuinely unfiltered/baseline-free page exists to compare timings or request outcomes against. Blocked requests in this proxy also surface as HTTP 500 after roughly 1.3 s each, which is a harness artifact rather than page behaviour, so measured latencies cannot be attributed to the reported product. Guidance on how to validate or refute a timing-only incorrect-blocking claim under this limitation is missing.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported breakage (product carousel replaced by two "Component static resources failed to be loaded" strings) reproduces, but it is not caused by the filter lists:⁠ the same failed component appears in the experiment phase with no rules applied, the component's own CSS/JS return 200, and no captured rule blocks them. A scoped exception for the blocked Evidon consent script did not restore the carousel, so no filter rule could be validated and none is proposed.

## Still visible after the rule

- Tile 1:⁠ directly beneath the Black Friday deal-category icon row — The first “Component static resources failed to be loaded” diagnostic appears above a large empty band where deal/product content should render; the featured-products carousel and product cards are missing.
- Tile 1:⁠ below the first failed component band, above the Feedback/Need Help bar — A second “Component static resources failed to be loaded” diagnostic appears with another large blank content band; the page module is not rendered.
- Tile 2:⁠ below the Feedback/Need Help bar, above the doorbuster FAQ — A third “Component static resources failed to be loaded” diagnostic appears with a large blank band; a further content module is missing.
- Tile 3:⁠ below the doorbuster FAQ list, above the footer — A fourth “Component static resources failed to be loaded” diagnostic appears with a large blank band before the footer; the content module is missing.
- Blank white band immediately above the footer, below the FAQ/content area — Empty white region where a page component failed to render, matching the repeated failed-component symptom described by the reporter; this tile shows the lower portion of that missing-content area, with no diagnostic text visible within the tile itself.
- and 2 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Missing information

- No usable unfiltered control and no reporter-profile parity in the adguard_cli route: In this adguard_cli run every browser session goes through the filtering proxy:⁠ launch_browser refuses settings on extension "none" ("A control session runs no blocker and takes no settings"), while extension "prepared" launches a pinned browser extension (v5.5.2.3) whose launch answer reports settingsVerified=false, so the issue's settings import URL (reported_on_current) was never actually applied. apply_rule also refused the prepared session with cli_route_session_required. The only unfiltered comparison available was phase A of the apply_rule experiment (appliedRules [⁠]⁠), which still had the proxy's content script and the AdGuard Extra user script injected, so a cause located in those injections cannot be excluded.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"83567878c2709f929232342c71ece1909e5cb45591b85ddacfd7ad67048abb66"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report is about the signed-in account page www⁠.yubico.com/tw/store/account/, whose account navigation list is missing in the reporter's "AdGuard on" screenshot; that URL answers 302 twice into ecom.login.yubico.com/signin (a sign-in wall the runner cannot pass), so the symptom could not be observed or fixed and no culprit rule exists. On every reachable yubico page under the reporter's exact filter set only Google Ads requests and Cookiebot's consent config are blocked (the consent banner still renders and its underlay is dismissable), and no element-hiding rule acts, so no rule is proposed.

## Missing information

- No way to reach a reporter-authenticated page (sign-in-gated reported URL): The reported URL https:⁠//www⁠.yubico.com/tw/store/account/ is a signed-in account page:⁠ it answers 302 to /tw/store/account/signin/?redirectUrl=%2Ftw%2Fstore%2Faccount%2F, then 302 to ecom.login.yubico.com/signin (HAR artifact:⁠har:⁠2502defc-2c57-42a2-b778-1a63d01ba83c). The run instruction and the tool set give no way to authenticate (no credentials, and interact_page refuses sign-in controls), and the full-page vision classified the capture as a sign_in_wall; the runner states it cannot sign in. Therefore the reporter-defined symptom (the account navigation menu of the signed-in account page) cannot be observed in either the filtered baseline or any candidate phase, and no rule can be validated against it. The issue also carries no reporter settings import URL, so only the issue-derived profile is available.

Thank you for taking the time to read this. I have the paid version of Adguard and I'm having problems with a few apps. My issues are not with any browser or any websites. The main culprit is an app called FreeReels. I actually contacted y'all about this app and this issue a few days ago. After I contacted y'all, the ad blocking worked much better. While no ads would pop up, a blank screen would pop up every so often. However I was able to immediately tap the "x" at the top of the screen and get back to watching whatever I was watching. So the interruptions were minimal. But now the ad blocking isn't working at all. I'm getting full video ads/redirects every few minutes. I haven't changed any settings. I've only recently updated my Adguard. Also, I have Rush Drama and ShortBox. They just simply won't work at all. I. Keep getting "no network" or something similar whenever I try to use those apps. MeloShort and PineBox are two other apps I have, but the ad blocking seems to be mostly working with them. Also I have a mindless game I like to play to pass the time every so often that also contains ads, but all those ads are blocked completely and perfectly. Fixed upstream, pending the extension release

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's highlighted element is cricinfo's app-download row ("Download the Android and iOS apps for a better experience."). The repository already carries an exact rule for it in AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt line 4782, and applying that rule hides the element with the page intact, so no new rule is needed — the reporter needs the filter version that contains it.

## Still visible after the rule

- Article footer between the share/heart row and the Terms of Use/Privacy Policy/Feedback links — A full-width blank reserved band remains at the location where the app-download promotion row appears in the reporter's example. No download text, Android/iOS links, label, or frame is visible in the gap, but the vertical spacing is visibly larger than ordinary section gaps on the page.
- Document y=16152..16964 — Full-width empty light-grey reserved block between the share/heart row and the Terms of Use / Privacy Policy / Feedback footer links, at the app-download promotion location; no app-download text, Android link, iOS link, or creative is visible.

Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — mavikol.com article pages carry two self-promotional "Google ile Bizi Tercih Edin / Bizi Seçin" cards in the reading flow (the element the reporter crossed out twice); one domain-scoped element-hiding rule removes both and apply_rule verified the page stays intact with no leftover space. Proposed in AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt, which the run instruction names for site self-promotion. ## Rule `mavikol.com##aside[aria-label^="Google Tercih Edilen Kaynak"]` ## Policy rationale The reported element promotes the site's own Google preferred-source status with no third-party compensation, so it is self-promotion; the run instruction directs self-promotion rules to AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt and the filter policy lists blocking site self-promotion as that filter's purpose. The report is neither a paywall, an anti-adblock wall, nor a scam/phishing page, so none of the instruction's close-or-hand-off rules applies. A verified domain-scoped element-hiding rule exists, meets the policy quality requirements (no JS rule, cosmetic only) and matches the reporter-defined target in both screenshots. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1513043f55736b789e5d72487d79eabb479f6ad2/AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt) At the end of the file: self-promo.txt is not sorted:⁠ the 'Self-promo - Regular rules' section ends at line 4345 and every newer per-site rule is appended at the end of the file (lines 4735-6255), each preceded by a `!+ NOT_OPTIMIZED` marker that the maintainer should add above the new line. ## Missing information - Reporter settings import cannot be applied on the locked adguard_cli route: The issue carries a settings import URL (reports.adguard.com/settings/import.html?...&⁠filters=1.2.3.4.11.13.17.18.19.20.21.22.25.118.208.255.257&⁠custom_filters=...), but in the locked adguard_cli environment launch_browser rejects `settings` for an extension:⁠"none" session ("settings:⁠ Invalid type:⁠ Expected never but received Object") and offers no way to apply the reporter profile to the CLI proxy browser. The locked baseline also reports skippedSources for EasyPrivacy, Online Malicious URL Blocklist, Phishing URL Blocklist, uBlock Badware risks and the three custom subscriptions, so reporter parity was not reproducible. Additionally, no lint_rule tool was offered by this run, so the candidate was not linted against the repository linter; validation relied on apply_rule only. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45775361072 Automated analysis against filters at `1513043`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Regarding incorrect blocking, as reported here - https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/213168#issuecomment-7182198686
This issue should already be fixed. However, due to Google's policies, MV3 extensions cannot update filters dynamically, so the updated rules will be included in one of the upcoming extension updates.

In the meantime, please add the following rule to your user rules:
```adblock
facebook.com,facebookwkhpilnemxj7asaniu7vnjjbiltxjqhye3mhbshg7kx5tfyd.onion#@%#//scriptlet('trusted-replace-xhr-response', '/\{"node":\{"__typename":"MarketplaceFeedAdStory"[^\n]+?"cursor":(?:null|"\{[^\n]+?\}"|[^\n]+?MarketplaceSearchFeedStoriesEdge")\}/g', '{}', '/api/graphql')
```

issue.body: ### Prerequisites - [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material, otherwise use [NSFW-specific form](./new?template=bug_report_NSFW.yml); - [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue; - [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date; - [x] Browser version is up-to-date; - [x] If the site or app is broken, disabling AdGuard protection resolves an issue. ### What product do you use? AdGuard Browser Extension ### AdGuard version 5.5.3.3 (MV3 browser extension) ### What type of problem have you encountered? Website or app doesn't work properly ### Which browser(s) do you use? Chrome ### Which device do you use? Desktop ### Where is the problem encountered? https://speedof.me/m/ ### Ad Blocking AdGuard Base filter ### Privacy _No response_ ### Social Widgets _No response_ ### Annoyances AdGuard Cookie Notices filter, AdGuard Popups filter, AdGuard Other Annoyances filter ### Security _No response_ ### Other _No response_ ### DNS filters _No response_ ### Language-specific _No response_ ### What Stealth Mode options do you have enabled? _No response_ ### Add your comment and screenshots Hi, the recent filter changes associated with #245320 break the mobile speed test on SpeedOf.Me: https://speedof.me/m/ (build 3.205.2509). The START TEST control disappears, so visitors cannot start a speed test. With AdGuard disabled, the control is visible again. ### Rules responsible This rule hides the mobile START TEST control and the introductory text: ```text speedof.me###intro_container > div:not(.intro-group-container, .intro-dots) ``` This rule also matches the entire mobile results panel because `#result_container` is missing from its exceptions: ```text speedof.me##.middle-container > div:not(#progress_container, #share_container, #history_container, #intro_container) ``` ### Reproduction 1. Open https://speedof.me/m/ at a mobile viewport (390 × 844 in this reproduction). 2. Enable AdGuard with the filters listed above and the current published speedof.me rules. 3. Reload: the START TEST control and introductory text are missing. 4. Disable AdGuard and reload: START TEST and the introductory text return. Captured on October 28, 2026 using Chromium 143.0.7499.169 with AdGuard Browser Extension MV3 v5.5.3.3 at a mobile viewport. These are desktop Chrome captures of the mobile site, not captures from an Android or iOS device. Enabled filters: AdGuard Base 2.4.93.84, Cookie Notices 2.0.95.55, Popups 2.0.84.8, and Other Annoyances 2.0.48.76. The current published speedof.me rules from AdguardFilters revision `5a6d91f` were also loaded as user rules because bundled lists can lag the repository. No additional experimental blocking rules were used. Also reproduced with Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.73 on macOS ARM64 at 390 × 844 using the same published rules. With only the intro-container rule exempted, START TEST returned and a real test completed, but the results panel and Repeat control remained hidden. Please revise the rules to preserve the START TEST control and mobile results panel. ### House promotions Separately, some placements promote SpeedOf.Me's own API, MCP integration, and connection certificate. These are promotions for the site's own services without third-party compensation. Could you review their treatment under the Base-filter policy concerning a site's own advertising? https://adguard.com/kb/general/ad-filtering/filter-policy/#limitations-and-exceptions Compensated affiliate offers have a different classification. ### Screenshots AdGuard enabled: START TEST and the introductory content are missing. AdGuard disabled: START TEST and the introductory content are visible. ### Privacy - [x] I agree to follow this condition

> 
> opositors.cat is a public information portal about civil-service exams (oposicions) in Catalonia, Spain. It lists official job calls from public administrations with links to the official sources. It does not ask for passwords or payment data and does not imitate any other site. It is hosted on Vercel; Google Safe Browsing and Yandex Safe Browsing do not list it.

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

<details>
<summary>Detailed description for iOS users</summary>

1. Install [**Usercripts**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/userscripts/id1463298887) app
2. Enable **Usercripts** extension in Safari settings
	* iOS 18+: `System settings` => `Apps` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	* iOS 17 and older: `System settings` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	Find **Usercripts**, enable it and allow `On other sites` permission
4. Open the [tinyShield ](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@list-kr/tinyshield@latest/dist/tinyShield.user.js) userscript URL in browser
5. Press the extensions icon in the address bar of Safari and select Userscripts 
6. Tap to install
7. In opened popup, scroll down and press Install button
8. Done.

</details>

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/issues).

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported blank idnes.cz page did not reproduce with the reporter's AdGuard filter set:⁠ behind the AdGuard CLI baseline the reported discussion URL first 302-redirects to the site's Didomi consent wall and then loads the full discussion page, and the homepage renders fully too (desktop and 375x812 mobile viewports). No applied rule from Base/Tracking/Mobile Ads/Mail Tracking removes page content, so no rule change is written; the iOS Safari execution model and the reporter's third-party EasyList Czech and Slovak could not be tested here.

## Missing information

- Reporter's EasyList Czech and Slovak is not part of the locked baseline: select_environment returned filterBaseline.skippedSources = [⁠{kind:⁠ third_party_catalog, reportedName:⁠ "EasyList Czech and Slovak"}]⁠. The reporter enabled that list on iOS, and the reported blank page could come from a rule in it, but the run cannot load it (official filters are Base 2, Tracking 3, Mobile Ads 11, Mail Tracking 25), so the blank-page symptom cannot be attributed to or cleared of that source.
- AdGuard for iOS / Safari execution model not reproducible in the locked environment: The report is from AdGuard for iOS v4.5.26 with Advanced protection enabled, but the locked adguard_cli environment executes the shared lists through the AdGuard CLI filtering proxy in Chromium (desktop and mobile 375x812 viewports). Safari's content-blocker conversion and the iOS app's own network path cannot be observed here, so a defect that only appears in that execution model cannot be reproduced or ruled out by this run. The engine also does not report the HTML-filtering ($$) and $replace rules that could alter a document body on idnes.cz.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — emailtooltester.com keeps a fixed cookie-consent bar ("We use cookies …" + OK) across the bottom of the viewport, unhandled by the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter and uncovered by any existing rule (the site has no rules in the repo). The domain-scoped element-hiding rule emailtooltester.com#⁠#⁠#⁠tt-cookie-notice was verified with apply_rule:⁠ bar visible before, hidden after, symptom resolved, page integrity intact, no residue. ## Rule `emailtooltester.com###tt-cookie-notice` ## Policy rationale Run instruction policy:⁠ the report is a cookie-notice annoyance (AdGuard Cookie Notices filter scope), not a paywall, an anti-adblock wall or self-promotion, so no listed rule closes it or hands it to a maintainer. The notice is served from the page's own HTML/CSS with no gated function behind it, so a standard domain-scoped element-hiding rule implements it without breaking site behaviour. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/fb6ae22d4e02e0b85402a5f13423618a75625ac3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Regular rules`, before [line 407](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/fb6ae22d4e02e0b85402a5f13423618a75625ac3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L407). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

<details>
<summary>Detailed description for iOS users</summary>

1. Install [**Usercripts**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/userscripts/id1463298887) app
2. Enable **Usercripts** extension in Safari settings
	* iOS 18+: `System settings` => `Apps` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	* iOS 17 and older: `System settings` => `Safari` => `Extensions`
	Find **Usercripts**, enable it and allow `On other sites` permission
4. Open the [tinyShield ](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@list-kr/tinyshield@latest/dist/tinyShield.user.js) userscript URL in browser
5. Press the extensions icon in the address bar of Safari and select Userscripts 
6. Tap to install
7. In opened popup, scroll down and press Install button
8. Done.

</details>

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/List-KR/tinyShield/issues).

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — easydmarc.com still shows its own cookie-consent bar (fixed white bottom bar with an "Agree" button, `section.cookie-consent`) because no filter covers the site. Fix:⁠ add `easydmarc.com` to the existing 240-domain shared rule `…##.cookie-consent` on line 75 of AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (under the comment `! ##.cookie-consent`), per the contributing guide adding the domain at the beginning of the cosmetic rule's domain list; the scoped candidate `easydmarc.com##.cookie-consent` validated verified with the page left intact. ## Rule `easydmarc.com##.cookie-consent` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy lists no rule that closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall, not self-promotion and not a scam page — it is an ordinary cookie-consent notice, which the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to hide. The maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them, but not the ones grouped by project' applies:⁠ line 75 of cookies_specific.txt is a cross-site shared rule for `.cookie-consent`, so the reported domain is added to it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a67dd31e8b1bc68b2d93571b8f584eb48143c4b2/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 75](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/a67dd31e8b1bc68b2d93571b8f584eb48143c4b2/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L75). ## Screenshots

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

Fallback — The page refused to load in the run browser:⁠ main document returned HTTP 403

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — quizlet.com/de shows an unblocked Ketch cookie-consent overlay (div.ketch-fixed); the repository already hides this exact Ketch element with the shared rule `…,equifax.ca##.ketch-fixed` (AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt line 131), so the fix is adding quizlet.com to that shared domain list. The candidate could not be verified:⁠ three navigation attempts to the reported URL all returned HTTP 403 with a captcha-challenge URL, exhausting browser access, so no apply_rule phases ran and the rule is passed to a maintainer for review.

## Candidate for review

`tasteofhome.com,azul.com,singlestore.com,ngrok.com,priceline.com.au,tvland.com,tennischannel.com,thesportsmanchannel.com,poptv.com,outdoorchannel.com,logotv.com,cmt.com,ksbw.com,kmbc.com,mynbc5.com,koat.com,ketv.com,kcci.com,gulfcoastnewsnow.com,wapt.com,watch.dropout.tv,larsondoors.com,equifax.ca,quizlet.com##.ketch-fixed`

AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt

Not verified: No browser validation was possible:⁠ open_page to https:⁠//quizlet.com/de returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare captcha-challenge URL in all three attempted sessions (desktop/de-DE, desktop/en-US, mobile/de-DE with reject), and the third attempt exhausted the target's browser-access budget, so apply_rule could not run any before/after phase and the session's report_finding/apply_rule tools are gated closed. The candidate rests on the reporter screenshot (div.ketch-fixed, inset 0, z-index 2147483647, 'Powered by Ketch', Reject All/Customize/Accept All) plus the repository's existing shared Ketch overlay rule; whether hiding .ketch-fixed alone leaves a body scroll lock or inside the overlay leaves page residue on quizlet.com, and whether a Ketch boot-script network rule is the better fix there, was never observable.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://opositors.cat/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopositors.cat%2F)

### Comment
> False positive: opositors.cat is listed as Phishing since 2026-11-21 (see https://reports.adguard.com/en/opositors.cat/report.html).
> 
> opositors.cat is a public information portal about civil-service exams (oposicions) in Catalonia, Spain. It lists official job calls from public administrations with links to the official sources. It does not ask for passwords or payment data and does not imitate any other site. It is hosted on Vercel; Google Safe Browsing and Yandex Safe Browsing do not list it.
> 
> With AdGuard DNS (Default server, set as Private DNS on Android), Chrome shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR because the domain resolves to the AdGuard block page.
> 
> Steps to reproduce: use AdGuard DNS Default server, open https://opositors.cat/
> 
> Please remove opositors.cat from the phishing category. Thank you.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)

### Comment
> False positive: opositors.cat is listed as Phishing since 2026-11-21 (see https://reports.adguard.com/en/opositors.cat/report.html).
> 
> opositors.cat is a public information portal about civil-service exams (oposicions) in Catalonia, Spain. It lists official job calls from public administrations with links to the official sources. It does not ask for passwords or payment data and does not imitate any other site. It is hosted on Vercel; Google Safe Browsing and Yandex Safe Browsing do not list it.

> With AdGuard DNS (Default server, set as Private DNS on Android), Chrome shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR because the domain resolves to the AdGuard block page.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kinetyka.pl serves its own persistent cookie-consent dialog (#⁠kt-cookie-bar, "Twoje ustawienia prywatności" with "Tylko niezbędne"/"Akceptuję analityczne", fixed bottom-right, 500x172) straight in the page HTML, so no Cookie Notices rule covers it. Adding kinetyka.pl#⁠#⁠#⁠kt-cookie-bar to AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt was verified in the reporter's profile:⁠ the bar is present before and gone after, page intact. ## Rule `kinetyka.pl###kt-cookie-bar` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is an annoyance:⁠ a first-party cookie-consent notice that the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter does not block. Indeterminate — The anti-adblock "Ads Detected!!!" overlay the reporter photographed did not reproduce:⁠ with the reporter's own filter lists the page loads (HTTP 200), the site's CHP Ads Block Detector markup and bait are present and the detector even adds its show class, yet the overlay never renders (display none, 0x0, full-page and viewport vision both show an undimmed page across reload, waits and scrolling), and no cosmetic rule from the baseline acted on it. Recommend closing as not reproducible; note that BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt line 901 already lists broadbottomvillage.co.uk in the shared rule `body > #page + div[id][class*=" "]`, whose selector matches this overlay wrapper, and that no detector script request exists because the detector logic is inline in the served HTML.

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ it is not a paywall and not a scam/phishing page, and the report was actually checked live rather than being dismissed on its label. The reported symptom is absent on the successfully loaded reported page in the reporter-parity filtered session, so no rule is needed and generations stays allowed; the anti-adblock gate ("write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script") was never reached because no rule is proposed. Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Issue #⁠248253 (aniwaffle.com, T:⁠ Annoyance from AdGuard for iOS) is the site's own fixed analytics cookie-consent bar over the landing page hero. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule in the AdGuard Cookie Notices file was validated:⁠ the bar is visible without it and gone with it, with the page layout, nav, hero and scrolling intact. ## Rule `aniwaffle.com##section.prelaunch-consent` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie notice, which the run instruction's filter policy assigns to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter ('This filter is designed to block both cookie notices and requests from cookie management platforms'); hiding is the policy's stated first method when the site needs no cookie decision for content. No policy rule blocks it:⁠ it is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (the page shows no detector script and no wall asking to disable the ad blocker), and not self-promotion. The agent never closes issues, and nothing here requires a maintainer handoff because the rule was validated in the browser. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1a8c389c47f13b087b5e420614c3f19bec79b8bc/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) Under the heading `! issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://countly.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcountly.com%2F)

### Comment
> countly.com, our company website, does not resolve on AdGuard DNS, so visitors get "This site can't be reached". It resolves normally on other resolvers and on AdGuard's non-filtering DNS (see the screenshots).
> 
> ```
> $ dig +short countly.com @94.140.14.14
> 0.0.0.0
> $ dig +short countly.com @1.1.1.1
> 104.21.9.244
> 172.67.161.200
> ```
> 
> It is blocked by these rules in SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers_firstparty.txt:
> 
> ```
> ! countly.com
> ||countly.
> ||countly-
> ```
> 
> `||countly.` matches every hostname that starts with `countly.`, so it blocks the entire countly.com domain and all of its subdomains, not a specific tracking host.
> 
> Please unblock the countly.com domain, for example with `@@||countly.com^`, or narrow these two rules.

```
Username: @ar2rsawseen
```

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://countly.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcountly.com%2F)

### Comment
> countly.com, our company website, does not resolve on AdGuard DNS, so visitors get "This site can't be reached". It resolves normally on other resolvers and on AdGuard's non-filtering DNS (see the screenshots).
> 
> ```
> $ dig +short countly.com @94.140.14.14
> 0.0.0.0
> $ dig +short countly.com @1.1.1.1
> 104.21.9.244
> 172.67.161.200
> ```
> 
> It is blocked by these rules in SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers_firstparty.txt:
> 
> ```
> ! countly.com
> ||countly.
> ||countly-
> ```
> 
> `||countly.` matches every hostname that starts with `countly.`, so it blocks the entire countly.com domain and all of its subdomains, not a specific tracking host.
> 
> Please unblock the countly.com domain, for example with `@@||countly.com^`, or narrow these two rules.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://countly.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcountly.com%2F)

### Comment
> countly.com, our company website, does not resolve on AdGuard DNS, so visitors get "This site can't be reached". It resolves normally on other resolvers and on AdGuard's non-filtering DNS (see the screenshots).
> 
> ```
> $ dig +short countly.com @94.140.14.14
> 0.0.0.0
> $ dig +short countly.com @1.1.1.1
> 104.21.9.244
> 172.67.161.200
> ```
> 
> It is blocked by these rules in SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers_firstparty.txt:
> 
> ```
> ! countly.com
> ||countly.
> ||countly-
> ```
> 
> `||countly.` matches every hostname that starts with `countly.`, so it blocks the entire countly.com domain and all of its subdomains, not a specific tracking host.
> 
> Please unblock the countly.com domain, for example with `@@||countly.com^`, or narrow these two rules.

```
Username: @ar2rsawseen
```


### Screenshots
<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 1</summary>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/buk0xdmfxzk8kk8swoosso0ww44csggippubwdmrds.png?nc=1)
</details>
<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 2</summary>

  ![Screenshot 2](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/t9r4bftse684go0oow44480o8cgsoocgpv5faelfxc.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/hjv6248km1w04ookw0ooocoo0sc88ss5ef2vja5dog.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

| Information | Value |
|-------------|-------|
AdGuard product: | AdGuard DNS
DNS setup: | dig 9.10.6 (direct query to the resolver)
DNS server: | AdGuard DNS Default server
System version: | `macOS 27.0.1`
Browser: | None (DNS lookup with dig 9.10.6)

comment.body:
Thanks, but this isn't about our own access: we can use any resolver we like. The problem is
our visitors. Everyone using AdGuard DNS, AdGuard Home or the AdGuard browser extension
can't open countly.com at all, and we can't change their DNS settings.

`||countly.` matches the company website itself, not a tracking host, so the site is
unreachable for every AdGuard user. Your triage bot reached the same conclusion above and
suggested `@@||countly.com^` in tracking_servers_firstparty.txt.

Could you reopen this and add that exception, or narrow the rule? Happy to open a PR with the
one-line change if that's easier.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://countly.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcountly.com%2F)

### Comment
> countly.com, our company website, does not resolve on AdGuard DNS, so visitors get "This site can't be reached". It resolves normally on other resolvers and on AdGuard's non-filtering DNS (see the screenshots).
> 
> ```
> $ dig +short countly.com @94.140.14.14
> 0.0.0.0
> $ dig +short countly.com @1.1.1.1
> 104.21.9.244
> 172.67.161.200
> ```
> 
> It is blocked by these rules in SpywareFilter/sections/tracking_servers_firstparty.txt:
> 
> ```
> ! countly.com
> ||countly.
> ||countly-
> ```
> 
> `||countly.` matches every hostname that starts with `countly.`, so it blocks the entire countly.com domain and all of its subdomains, not a specific tracking host.
> 
> Please unblock the countly.com domain, for example with `@@||countly.com^`, or narrow these two rules.

```
Username: @ar2rsawseen
```


### Screenshots
<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 1</summary>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/buk0xdmfxzk8kk8swoosso0ww44csggippubwdmrds.png?nc=1)
</details>
<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 2</summary>

  ![Screenshot 2](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/t9r4bftse684go0oow44480o8cgsoocgpv5faelfxc.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

<details>
  <summary>Screenshot 1 with AdGuard disabled</summary>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/hjv6248km1w04ookw0ooocoo0sc88ss5ef2vja5dog.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

### System configuration

| Information | Value |
|-------------|-------|
AdGuard product: | AdGuard DNS
DNS setup: | dig 9.10.6 (direct query to the resolver)
DNS server: | AdGuard DNS Default server
System version: | `macOS 27.0.1`
Browser: | None (DNS lookup with dig 9.10.6)

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ae0125c252628088516a4e37264121cf523f417b1ffef3dd24fc3699e9d52c49"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported defect is Suntago's own full-screen "Black Weekend" promo popup (#⁠bigPromoModal), which also locks page scroll through html.-modalOpen; plain element hiding removes the popup but leaves the homepage unscrollable with no close control. The rule that both drops the popup and releases the lock needs #⁠bigPromoModal ⁠> .c-modal_overlay in its selector list, but the run's candidate attempts ran out before that version could be verified, so it is handed to a maintainer for AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt.

## Candidate for review

`suntago.com#$#html.-modalOpen, #bigPromoModal, #bigPromoModal > .c-modal_overlay { overflow: visible !important; top: 100000px !important; }`

AnnoyancesFilter/Other/sections/self-promo.txt

Not verified: Validation of the simplest rule (suntago.com#⁠#⁠#⁠bigPromoModal) passed the vision review and the experiment, but the captured phase-C DOM still carried <⁠html class="... -modalOpen"⁠>, so the site rule html.-modalOpen { overflow:⁠ hidden } keeps the document unscrollable while the popup's own close button is hidden (a wheel scroll in the baseline lane left scrollY at 0). The CSS-injection rule that adds html.-modalOpen was then rejected for ad layout residue:⁠ the dialog was pushed off-screen but its fixed backdrop stayed over the page (.c-modal_overlay, position fixed, inset 0, rgba(32,24,59,0.75), backdrop-filter blur(12px), direct child of a modal with transform:⁠none, so the viewport is its containing block). The rule above adds that overlay to the selector list; remainingCandidateAttempts reached 0 before it could be validated.

## Still visible after the rule

- Full viewport above the cookie bar (y≈0–795px):⁠ site header strip, left-hand hero heading and orange CTA button, right-hand promo card panel — The entire homepage is still covered by a translucent dark, heavily blurred full-screen layer:⁠ the header, the hero heading with its CTA and the right-hand card are dimmed and illegible, and the page behind cannot be seen or used. The 'Black Weekend w Suntago!' dialog panel itself is not rendered visibly in this state (apparently pushed off-screen), but its full-viewport dim/blur overlay remains over the hero region, so the homepage content the reporter could not see is still withheld and unreadable.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45853116490

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — strelec.ucoz.ru shows a promobox.cc ad banner (the one in the reporter's screenshot) built by its own promobox script, plus a right-sidebar "Реклама" ad panel left empty/broken by filtering; one domain-scoped cosmetic rule hides both and was verified in the AdGuard extension baseline (symptom resolved, page integrity intact). ## Rule `strelec.ucoz.ru##.promobox-inbody, table:has(> tbody > tr > td > center > a[href^="//clck.yandex.ru/"])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The run instruction states that ads for other companies get a rule like any other ad, including ads a site serves from its own host — promobox.cc is a third-party ad network banner delivered from the site's own path /.s/src/adv_scripts/static/promobox/. No blocking rule of the policy applies:⁠ this is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall (the page applies no detector and the session reported antiAdblockDetected false), and not the site's own self-promotion. No existing shared rule covers the case, so a new per-site rule is written instead of extending a family:⁠ searches for .promobox-inbody, .promobox, .js-teasers-wrapper and the urlPatterns promobox / adv_scripts / adv/dummy returned no applicable multi-domain rule (the only .promobox hit is an unrelated prepscholar subscription rule). The policy's traffic threshold and final decision for a site-specific rule rest with the filter developers; the site is a long-running ucoz-hosted Russian software portal included in the Russian filter scope. ## Place in the list [CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f30894403e94ce5e9d5479e55d9cf329b741f11a/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt) Under the heading `! NOTE: Specific rules`, before [line 17](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f30894403e94ce5e9d5479e55d9cf329b741f11a/CyrillicFilters/RussianFilter/sections/specific.txt#L17). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/45877961901 Automated analysis against filters at `f308944`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Trackers) [https://t3.codes/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ft3.codes%2F) ### Comment > Please add `||ingest.t3.codes^` to the AdGuard DNS filter (and EasyPrivacy if relevant). > > **What it is:** `ingest.t3.codes` is the analytics endpoint of T3 Code, an open-source desktop app for coding agents. It is a first-party proxy in front of PostHog: the app POSTs events to `https://ingest.t3.codes/batch/`. Telemetry is on by default. > > **Sources:** > - Telemetry docs: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/docs/user/telemetry.md > - `apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts`: `T3CODE_POSTHOG_HOST` defaults to `https://ingest.t3.codes`, events are sent to `/batch/` > > **Why existing rules miss it:** it is a custom subdomain proxied through Cloudflare, with no CNAME to posthog.com, so PostHog rules and CNAME uncloaking don't catch it. It is not in the AdGuard DNS filter or EasyPrivacy as of 2026-11-18. > > **Screenshot:** the AdGuard DNS Default server (94.140.14.14) blocks google-analytics.com (0.0.0.0) but resolves ingest.t3.codes, and a request over AdGuard DNS-over-HTTPS reaches the endpoint. > > **Breakage:** none expected. The app works normally with this host blocked. Please block only this subdomain, not t3.codes. ### Screenshots

Validated fix (apply_rule:⁠ verified, page integrity intact, symptom resolved):⁠ add smailpro.com to the existing shared rule at BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt line 4615 — solarmovie.fi,flixtor.mov,1movies.bz,movhub.ws,yflix.to#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="text-center"]⁠:⁠has(a[⁠href*="?utm_source="]⁠) — so it becomes smailpro.com#⁠#⁠div[⁠class^="text-center"]⁠:⁠has(a[⁠href*="?utm_source="]⁠). ## Rule `smailpro.com##div[class^="text-center"]:has(a[href*="?utm_source="])` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a website-filtering ad report for smailpro.com; the screenshot target is a third-party sponsored AccsZone placement (rel="sponsored", utm-tagged accszone.com link), which the run instruction's policy covers as 'ads for other companies ... direct-sold banners, sponsored placements'. It is not the site's own self-promotion (a third party pays for the placement), not a paywall, and no anti-adblock wall was detected:⁠ get_applied_rules and apply_rule reported antiAdblockDetected false and the page shows no detector overlay. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — estadao.com.br/tecmundo shows ten empty 186px "PUBLICIDADE" ad containers plus a 300px grey PUBLICIDADE box whose ad scripts the baseline blocks; the rule estadao.com.br#⁠#⁠.ads-container, div:⁠has(⁠> .area-parallax-text-border) hides both, and the experiment leaves zero ad slots/labels with the page shortened by exactly their height. The vision review kept rejecting it only for blank whitespace that the DOM checks and its own settlement show is the site's own section spacing, so the unverified rule goes to a maintainer.

## Candidate for review

`estadao.com.br##.ads-container, div:has(> .area-parallax-text-border)`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule reported adElementStatus .ads-container visible (phase B) -⁠> hidden (phase C), pageIntegrity intact and observedDamage empty, but the dedicated vision review rejected the candidate as 'not_resolved' with adLayoutResidue present on all three runs, naming plain white bands between editorial sections as leftover ad space. The experiment's DOM checks contradict that:⁠ phase C has 0 visible .ads-container/parallax slots, 0 visible PUBLICIDADE labels, 0 ad-classed elements with layout, no content-column gap over 100px, and a 2175px shorter document against a 2160px ad footprint; the review's own settlement marks several of those same gaps unchanged_before. No rule could therefore be published as verified in this run.

## Still visible after the rule

- Directly below the blue TecMundo header, above the 'AO VIVO BLACK FRIDAY' banner — Empty white band spanning the page width directly under the TecMundo header. The first banner-ad slot shows no creative, PUBLICIDADE label, frame or placeholder block, only residual blank space.
- Blank band between the INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL carousel (Meta super IA article) and the VOXL section; tile landmark includes ‘Difícil imaginar...’ / ‘As notícias mais importantes sobre games num só lugar.’ — A visibly tall, full-width empty white banner area sits between the bottom carousel dots of the AI/Meta article card and the VOXL section. No ad creative or PUBLICIDADE label is visible; the reserved gap is larger than the ordinary spacing within the VOXL block, matching the leftover empty advertising footprint.
- Blank band between the INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL carousel (Meta super IA article) and the VOXL section; tile landmark includes ‘Difícil imaginar...’ / ‘As notícias mais importantes sobre games num só lugar.’ — The same tall, full-width empty white banner gap between the AI/Meta carousel and the VOXL section is visible in this overlapping tile. No ad creative or PUBLICIDADE label appears; it is a residual reserved advertising space.
- PRODUTO E REVIEW article list, below the row beginning 'É hoje! Live da virada do Estadão terá mais de 2.600 ofertas' — A very large empty white area follows the related-article row and continues to the bottom of the tile. No ad creative, PUBLICIDADE label, frame, or placeholder block is visible in this reserved gap.
- Above the BIG TECHS carousel dots and section heading, continuing the large blank band from the preceding live-article area — A visibly oversized empty reserved advertising gap/placeholder footprint above BIG TECHS. After the candidate, no PUBLICIDADE label, frame, or ad creative is visible; only a large blank white band remains, much taller than ordinary spacing between sections.

That view is unreachable here (the 出題開始 submit is refused), so apply_rule reported baseline_symptom_absent and no rule could be verified; a domain-scoped set-attr scriptlet is carried for maintainer review.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Report is an annoyance (cookie notice) filed from AdGuard for Windows, whose filtering runs in the desktop app's network filter, so it was analyzed in the locked adguard_cli environment (AdGuard CLI 1.4.13 proxy over the official-filter baseline). The reporter's browser (Chrome) and the Windows app itself were not executed; that provenance gap is kept. Baseline evidence:⁠ a fixed full-viewport overlay (data-testid="overlay-cookie-consents-modal") wraps <⁠dialog data-testid="cookie-consents-modal"⁠> with the Polish cookie notice and its three buttons, and while it is up body carries inline overflow:⁠hidden, locking scrolling. No third-party CMP host is involved, so the notice is first-party and must be handled through consent state rather than a vendor network rule. The published rule siepomaga.pl#⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('trusted-set-cookie','consents','…') is applied on the page but the notice still renders; rehearsal showed the site's own reject button clears the notice and the scroll lock and stores a persistent consents cookie, yet the notice returns after a reload — consistent with the stale static cookie value being re-injected on every load. So the fix records consent through the site's own handler instead of simulating a cookie value. Validation:⁠ apply_rule returned environmentExperiment "verified" with a bound visualReview "verified" (symptom resolved, pageIntegrity intact, adLayoutResidue absent, remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty); the fixed overlay height dropped from full viewport to \~55 px of ordinary sticky header and the donation page content stays legible. Placement:⁠ the site's rules live in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, so the new scriptlet goes directly below the site's existing scriptlet rule (line 3568 once inserted). (shortened; the full text is in the run artifacts)
